state: Existing I20 machinery records immutable captures and retains resource leases when a coordination participant launches. P6 requires maintained catalogue operations to check provenance, scope and lifecycle before using native handles; host callbacks have an owning-operation lifetime guard before entering authored code. Scoped handles may be returned, put in records or captured without a new static ownership regime, while out-of-scope or closed-handle use must fail dynamically. The explicit Q10 retention requirement concerns coordination participants. No whole-call lease requirement is stated for ordinary named functions. If every ordinary callable invocation leases its captures, a callable that closes its captured pool cannot finish: close waits for a lease released only after that same call returns. Removing coordination leases would violate the contract, so the ordinary-call wrapper is the disputed layer. Alternatives retain only ordinary capture metadata with leases at coordination/native boundaries and host lifetime guards, perform eager ordinary capture validation but no leases, or retain all resources across every callable invocation.

capture_scope.instructions: Which policy preserves required resource safety with the least additional ordinary-call semantics?

criteria.boundaries: Record captures without changing plain call behavior; let owned participants, native handle operations and host callback guards enforce their respective contracts.
criteria.validate: Add pre-body lifecycle validation to all resource-capturing ordinary functions but omit lease retention.
criteria.lease: Retain whole-invocation resource leases around ordinary function values as well as coordination participants.
